21340.testo: ReVive was born out of a desire to create more accessible and inclusive creative spaces, where making art is not limited by talent, financial resources or traditional ideas of what art should be or talk about. It is an invitation to look at the objects and materials around us with a different perspective, reconnecting with the joy of crafting and transforming what already exists. ✨ About the Project ReVive is a 10 day Youth Experiential Learning Program that wishes to bring together young queer people and allies from diverse backgrounds in a shared creative space to explore upcycled art and artistic expression through a hands on approach. The team aims to create a space where creativity can be explored freely, without pressure or expectations, offering the opportunity to experiment with discarded materials and objects. Through this process, you are invited to explore how creative practices can shape our experiences, being a tool to express ourselves, connect with others and perhaps see the world from different perspectives. From the very beginning, the experience is shaped together, creating community agreements to build a safer and braver space for living and working, while encouraging active participation, accountability, mutual support and collective care. For the team, living together is a very important part of the experience. This means sharing responsibilities, taking care of common spaces and each of us, in our own way, contributing to the atmosphere we want to create. This can be through daily tasks such as cleaning, tidying up, decorating the space, preparing breakfast, collaborating on creative projects or simply spending time together. By living and working together, everyone shares in the experience of being part of a collectively created community. The parts of an Erasmus+ project nobody tells you about before you go: https://youthworkshub.org/15126/ 🎯 Objectives 🌈 Create a safer and braver space for queer young people and allies to explore creativity through upcycled art and experience creation as an open process of experimentation 🤝 Form connections through shared creative experiences, embracing intersectionality and building a supportive community that starts during the project and continues growing as a creative network across Europe 🖌️ Support participants in developing their own creative language and ways of expressing themselves, strengthening their confidence and sense of ownership over their creative process ♻️ Rethink the creative potential of discarded materials, promoting more sustainable artistic practices and inspiring participants to see value in what is often overlooked or thrown away 🖼️ Organise a local exhibition in Riga during the Youth Exchange, celebrating the artworks developed during the project, as well as local actions in each partner country during the local action phase 🧠 The Learning Approach This learning programme follows an experiential learning approach and is highly participatory and interactive, giving you the chance for self reflection and self evaluation. This approach involves learning by doing and peer to peer learning, meaning learning from each other. Within the given context and given group, you are the actor of your own learning and creator of your own experience. The outcome of your experience depends solely on you, while guided and supported by the facilitators in correlation to the rest of the group. You are part of an intercultural environment and, as much as possible, an intersectional space, and you have the chance to work individually, in pairs, in small teams and in a big group. You are able to explore different forms of creative expression and sustainability, understand what creativity and collective creation mean to you, and find inspiration in yourself and your peers. ⏰ The working hours vary according to the needs of the group and the programme. European research and policy analysis show that climate change is already affecting young people's physical health, deepening social inequalities and adding emotional strain — including the growing phenomenon of eco-anxiety. The Council of Europe and the European Commission both stress that young people are experiencing, and will continue to bear, the brunt of worsening climate impacts, which makes climate action not only an environmental issue but a matter of intergenerational justice. At the same time, youth engagement is increasingly recognised as a decisive force in Europe's green transition. Through both formal pathways (schools, civic participation) and informal ones (community projects, youth work), young people bring creativity, fresh perspectives and a direct stake in long-term solutions. The Council of Europe's Recommendation on Young People and Climate Action goes further, insisting that young people be meaningfully included in climate decision-making, that young climate defenders be protected, and that the structural barriers keeping youth out of policy be removed. 30366.testo: A 7-day Erasmus+ training exploring dreamwork, embodiment, expressive arts and nature-based practices, offering experiential methods and tools for youth workers to bring into their work with young people and communities. It is dark, our eyes drop heavy, and behind them another world invites us in, no matter if we remember that world upon waking. As our bodies rest, our psyche takes us towards images, memories, emotions and stories that often remain outside our everyday awareness. Dreaming from the Mycelium of the Earth is an invitation. An invitation to become curious about the intelligence that lives beneath our usual ways of knowing. Like mycelium moving quietly beneath the forest floor, much of what shapes us remains unseen. An invitation to tend dreams as wild and meaningful parts of ourselves. An invitation to be guided by dreams, movement, art, imagination and nature — allowing them to move with us and within us. And an invitation to explore how these practices can enrich youth work and non-formal education, creating spaces where young people can deepen their relationship with themselves, their communities and the more-than-human world. Dreaming from the Mycelium of the Earth is a 7-day Erasmus+ training course combining dreamwork, embodiment, storytelling, poetry, expressive arts, deep imagination and ecological and nature-based education. The training will offer youth workers and other professionals working with people a space to first experience these approaches themselves and then explore how they can be adapted to their own educational contexts. We believe that meaningful youth work begins not only with methods, but also with the capacity of the practitioner to be present, listen, notice, imagine and create spaces where different ways of knowing and expressing ourselves are welcomed. Throughout the programme, participants will therefore move between personal experience, group learning and professional reflection: What does this practice awaken in me? What does it teach me as a facilitator? How could it support the young people and communities I work with? The deep winter landscape of rural Latvia will become part of our learning environment — a place for slowing down, listening, creating, moving and experimenting. We hope participants will leave with new resources, perspectives and practical methods that can be brought back into their youth work, educational activities and communities. DURING THE TRAINING WE WILL EXPLORE - dream-tending and approaches to working with dreams; - embodiment and somatic awareness; - movement and expressive arts; - storytelling and poetry; - deep imagination; - nature-based and experiential learning; - ecological awareness and relationship with the more-than-human world; - reflection and council practices; - intercultural learning; - resilience and self-care; - ways of adapting experiential and creative practices to youth work and non-formal education. The methodology will be highly experiential. Participants should be willing to engage actively in individual practices, group processes, creative exploration, time outdoors and reflection. YOUTH WORK & LEARNING An important part of the training will be exploring how creative, embodied and nature-based approaches can support contemporary youth work. Young people increasingly need spaces where they can slow down, reconnect with their bodies and creativity, explore identity and emotions, experience meaningful relationships and develop a deeper sense of belonging to their communities and the natural world. The training aims to expand the methodological toolbox of youth workers by introducing practices that can support self-expression, self-awareness, creativity, emotional resilience, connection, participation and ecological awareness. Participants will be invited to reflect on how the methods experienced during the programme can be adapted responsibly to different groups of young people and different educational and community contexts. The intention is therefore not to train participants to become therapists or dream analysts. Instead, we will explore dream, imagination, embodiment, art and nature as creative and educational resources within non-formal learning and youth work. WHO IS IT FOR? We are calling in people who work with people — those who create spaces for learning, growth, connection and transformation. The programme is particularly relevant for: youth workers, facilitators, educators, mentors, coaches, guides, artists, community workers and nature-based practitioners, as well as those whose work does not quite fit into a single box. You do not need to arrive as an expert, nor do you need previous experience with dreamwork or nature-based practices. We are more interested in your curiosity: your willingness to listen, experiment, participate fully and bring what you discover back into the communities and people you work with. Participants must: be 18 years or older; be able to communicate and participate in English; be willing to participate in the whole programme; be interested in applying or sharing the learning in their youth work, educational practice or communities; legally reside in one of the participating countries. Applications are open to residents of: Latvia, Romania, Cyprus, Italy, Iceland, Estonia, Czechia and Slovakia. 31254.testo: Y.E.S. is an international training course on developing inclusive youth projects, designing Erasmus+ funding applications and planning projects for diverse youth groups. The training will be in Russian. The training aims to develop participants’ practical skills in designing inclusive youth projects for diverse youth groups, preparing Erasmus+ funding applications and planning the successful implementation of their own projects. During the course, participants will explore the opportunities offered by the Erasmus+ programme, focusing on youth exchanges and training courses. They will learn how to choose the most appropriate project format for their ideas and how to develop a project from the initial analysis of the target group’s needs to the definition of objectives, methods and expected outcomes. The course will introduce participants to the logic of project development and the key elements of a funding application, ensuring a clear connection between identified needs, project objectives, planned activities, budget and evaluation. A particular focus will be placed on social inclusion and working with diverse youth groups. Participants will explore how to identify barriers to participation, take different needs into account at every stage of a project, and create accessible activities for young people with different abilities, backgrounds and levels of experience. They will learn how to adapt non-formal education methods, organise activities inclusively and provide appropriate support to participants. Participants will also develop their own project ideas, work on the key sections of an Erasmus+ funding application and identify the next steps towards preparing and implementing their projects. The training provides an opportunity to strengthen practical project development skills, exchange experiences with youth workers from different countries and explore opportunities for international cooperation within the Erasmus+ programme. The training is designed as a practical learning process that connects the principles of inclusion with the concrete stages of project development, from identifying needs and designing activities to preparing funding applications and planning implementation. Objectives of the training The main objective of the training is to develop participants’ competencies in designing inclusive youth projects, preparing Erasmus+ funding applications and planning activities that respond to the needs of diverse youth groups. By the end of the training, participants will: explore the opportunities offered by the Erasmus+ programme, including youth exchanges and training courses; learn how to choose the appropriate Erasmus+ project format for their ideas; understand the principles of social inclusion and identify barriers that may prevent young people from participating in projects; learn how to analyse the needs of a target group and translate them into clear project objectives; develop skills in selecting appropriate non-formal education methods and defining expected project outcomes; understand the structure of an Erasmus+ funding application and the connections between needs, objectives, activities, budget and evaluation; learn how to plan accessible activities for diverse youth groups with different abilities and levels of experience; explore how to adapt methods, organisational arrangements and participant support to different needs; develop their own project ideas and prepare key sections of an Erasmus+ funding application; identify the next steps towards preparing and implementing their projects; become more confident in applying the knowledge and methods gained during the training to their future youth work. Target group – the training is aimed at: youth workers; leaders of youth non-governmental organisations; educators and trainers; people interested in developing their own projects within the Erasmus+ programme; people who have experience or motivation to work with youth groups and are interested in inclusive youth work and international cooperation. Participants are expected to have experience or a willingness to work with youth groups, be ready to use non-formal education methods and actively participate in all course activities. They should be motivated to develop their professional skills in youth work and be willing to apply the knowledge gained during the training in their future activities and projects. Methodology The training focuses on practical learning, active participation and the application of non-formal education methods. Participants will explore the Erasmus+ programme, analyse the needs of different youth groups, examine the principles of social inclusion and work through the key stages of project development. The learning process will combine individual work, group activities, discussions, experience sharing and practical project development tasks. Participants will work on their own project ideas, define objectives and expected outcomes, select appropriate methods and develop key sections of a funding application. Particular attention will be given to ensuring that project activities are accessible and that the needs of diverse participants are considered throughout the project cycle. The methodology connects theoretical understanding with practical application, enabling participants to leave the training with a clearer understanding of the Erasmus+ programme and concrete foundations for developing their own inclusive youth projects.

31420.testo: Youth Exchange bringing 32 young people from Lithuania, Türkiye, Italy and Spain together to explore career paths, develop skills, build motivation and create career plans. Erasmus+ Youth Exchange taking place in Kaunas, Lithuania, from 18–27 November 2026. The project brings together 32 young people from Lithuania, Türkiye, Italy and Spain for an international learning experience focused on career development and personal growth. Many young people at the beginning of their careers struggle to identify a professional path that matches their interests, strengths and goals. They may lack knowledge about available opportunities, awareness of their competencies, or a clear plan for developing their skills. This can lead to uncertainty about their future, whether they are studying, working or not yet engaged in career activities. During the eight-day exchange, participants will explore different professional opportunities and career paths, assess their competencies and identify areas for improvement. Through interactive and inclusive non-formal learning activities, they will work on developing a positive mindset, discovering their career motivation and creating short- and long-term personal development plans. The project also focuses on the role of non-formal learning, mentorship and international experience in professional development. By bringing together young people from different countries, the exchange creates an opportunity to share experiences, approaches and perspectives on career choices while challenging stereotypes connected to professional paths. The project aims to have an impact beyond the mobility itself. Following the exchange, participants will establish Career Advancement Clubs in their home countries. These clubs will provide local spaces where young people can meet, exchange experiences, explore career opportunities, develop practical skills and support one another in achieving their professional goals. Through these follow-up activities, participants will transfer the knowledge and tools gained during the exchange to their local communities and adapt them to the needs of young people in their respective contexts.

Join a 2-9 month volunteering experience in rural Latvia. Support preschool children (ages 1.5–6) as they grow, play, and explore nature. Be part of daily preschool life and outdoor forest activities. Our project focuses on three big themes: green thinking & sustainability, social inclusion & community growth, and creative use of digital tools. Opportunity to work in the local Youth centre and High school. We offer a safe, inspiring space with passionate educators, nature all around, and freedom to shape your own experience. Some volunteers after the project have become excellent preschool teachers who went to study this field at the university, some took totally different paths, but all have learned and developed.

A person who wants to experience some type of mild Nordic weather living, meet spring with open arms and experience a summer of the unknown. If you feel ready for action and learning with some active and creative kids, then this is for you.
